cards.text: This letter goes to believers who've been through a lot, and the writer has just told them they need to persevere and not shrink back (Hebrews 10:32-39). Then the writer stops to say what faith is: "Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for…"

cards.question: Faith, the writer says, is the assurance of what we hope for. True or false: The writer says faith is also the certainty of what we can already see.

cards.text: Faith, the writer says, is why the ancients were commended. Commended! In all my years in the back of a junk drawer, the only one who ever complimented me was an expired coupon, and it complimented EVERYBODY.

cards.question: Before any names, the writer goes all the way back. By faith we understand the universe was formed at God's command. So what does the writer say about what everything we see was made out of?

answers.text: Not out of what was visible
Out of older things you could see
Out of leftover light from stars

cards.text: First name up: Abel, son of Adam and Eve (Genesis 4:1-2). By faith he offers God a better sacrifice than his brother Cain did.

cards.question: Abel's sacrifice was better than Cain's. By faith Abel was commended as ___ when God gave approval to his gifts.
True or false: The writer says that even though Abel is dead, by faith he still speaks.

cards.text: Next up: Enoch, Methuselah's father (Genesis 5:21). By faith Enoch was taken up so that he did not see death.
The writer quotes Genesis about Enoch: "He could not be found, because God had taken him away."

cards.question: True or false: Before Enoch was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God.
Then the writer says without faith it's impossible to please God. Anyone who approaches Him must believe that He ___ and that He ___ those who earnestly seek Him.

cards.text: Then comes Noah, Enoch's great-grandson (Genesis 5:21-29), warned about things not yet seen. Most of us hit snooze on a warning about something we can't even see yet, but Noah acts in godly fear.

cards.question: Noah's been warned about things not yet seen. In godly fear, what does he build?

answers.text: An ark to save his family
A city named for his son
A tower to reach the sky

cards.text: And by faith, the writer says, Noah condemned the world. One man, one ark, one big statement.

cards.question: Noah built the ark and condemned the world. What does the writer say Noah became heir of?

answers.text: The righteousness that comes by faith
The riches of the whole earth
The throne of a great kingdom

cards.text: Next name: Abraham, the man God promised to make into a great nation (Genesis 12:1-2). By faith, when he's called to go to a place he'd later receive as his inheritance, he obeys.

cards.question: True or false: Abraham obeyed and went, even though he didn't know where he was going.

cards.text: No map, no directions, and by faith Abraham ends up dwelling in the promised land as a stranger in a foreign country. Me? I live on a planet barely big enough for one bakery and I STILL double check which way the oven is.

cards.question: Abraham is in the promised land, living there as a stranger. What does he live in?

cards.text: Isaac and Jacob, his son and grandson (Genesis 21:3; 25:26), live in tents too, heirs with him of the same promise. Three generations in tents, friend, that's not camping anymore, that's a family tradition.

cards.question: Abraham's living in tents, but he's looking forward to the city with ___, whose architect and builder is God.

cards.text: Now Sarah, Abraham's wife (Genesis 17:15). She's barren and beyond the proper age, but by faith she's enabled to conceive a child.

cards.question: Sarah was past the age, and by faith she was enabled to conceive. What does the writer say was behind it?

answers.text: She considered God faithful to His promise
She asked a prophet to pray for her
She waited for a sign from heaven

cards.text: And so from one man, and he as good as dead, come descendants. Write that starting number down, friend: ONE.

cards.question: From Abraham, one man who was as good as dead, how many descendants come?

answers.text: As many as the stars and the sand
As many as the leaves on a tree
As many as the tribes of Israel

cards.text: Then the writer looks at all of them together. All these people died in faith, without having received the things they were promised.

cards.question: True or false: The writer says the people of faith on the list saw the promised things and welcomed them from afar.
The people of faith on the writer's list acknowledged they were strangers and exiles on the earth. The writer says people who talk like that are seeking what?

answers.text: A way back to their old home
A king to rule over them

cards.text: If those people of faith had been thinking of the country they left, they would have had the chance to go back. Me? Offer me my old spot in the junk drawer and I'm saying NO THANK YOU before you finish the sentence.

cards.question: Instead of the country they left, the people of faith on the writer's list were longing for a better country, a ___ one.
True or false: Because the people of faith on the writer's list longed for a heavenly country, God is ashamed to be called their God.

cards.text: And God has prepared a city for them. The writer isn't finished with this teaching yet, friend, so keep that apron on.
